page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration designed for balanced compute and memory workloads. The instance provision provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, running on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz. It is configured with 128 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache specifications include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 55 MB L3 cache. There are no bundled local storage devices or dedicated GPUs included with this instance type, requiring external persistent disks for storage needs.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier throughput across multi-threaded operations alongside constrained single-core processing capabilities. In raw compute tests, the system achieved a stress-ng multi-core metric of 42,996.45 and a PassMark CPU score of 38,099.23, placing it squarely in the middle tier of tested hardware. Single-core tests reveal limitations, with a Geekbench single-core score of 934.0 and weak single-threaded decompression metrics, although stress-ng single-core compute showed stronger synthetic performance. Cache-level read memory bandwidth reached 1,299.46 GB/sec, while uncached large-block read and write bandwidth measured 98.83 GB/sec and 44.29 GB/sec respectively.

The e2-standard-32 offers predictable cost efficiency for parallelized application architectures that do not rely on modern vector extensions such as AVX-512 or AMX. The instance maintains competitive throughput for distributed services, evidenced by 21.98 million Redis SET operations per second and static web serving throughput of 18.06 GB/sec. Workloads that match this profile include enterprise web serving, mid-sized database management systems, build and continuous integration pipelines, and general business application hosting.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-32 is a general-purpose compute instance equipped with 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 2.2 GHz x86_64 processor, paired with 128 GB of RAM. Designed without bundled local storage or GPUs, this instance maintains a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory allocation. Performance benchmarks place the instance within the middle tier for multi-core compute and data processing, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 38,099.23 and Redis throughput of 21.98 million operations per second. However, single-core processing remains constrained, as indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 934.0 and low single-thread compression speeds. Operating without advanced vector extensions such as AVX-512, the configuration functions as a cost-efficient resource tier for horizontal microservices, static web delivery, continuous integration builders, and parallelized database servers requiring consistent multi-threaded execution.
